maggie_cs: Quick heads up 1 BlueLeaf onboarding hit intermittent 429s during load testing. They deployed an ephemeral-token refresh per Lambda and saw bursts.
sam_customer: we observed 429s with Retry-After:3 after cold starts. Using node-sdk v1.2.0 on Lambda (us-east-1). Each function cold start renews token then fires ~20 concurrent generate calls.
indra_runtime: pattern sounds like token fanout + NAT amplification (many containers sharing NAT). Paste snippet?
sam_customer: logs:
2024-03-08T14:23:01Z func-start id=abc123
POST /v1/session/renew 200 id=abc123
POST /v1/generate -> 429 Retry-After: 3
retry x3 then 200
We saw ~60 concurrent generate calls from same egress IP.
maggie_cs: checklist: are tokens cached across invocations? TTL? region pinned?
sam_customer: TTL 45s, in-container cache only, low container reuse.
indra_runtime: short TTL + container churn explain renewals; serverless NAT concentrates concurrency onto few IPs -> route-level soft caps trigger 429s.
oncall-bot: oncall pinged.
maggie_cs: mitigations: 1) short-term: request temporary burst allowance for onboarding 2) app: increase token TTL to 5-10min or centralize token broker / shared cache (Redis) 3) SDK: enable sessionCache and set maxParallelRequests 4) infra: confirm XFF if behind proxy so throttles are per-tenant not per-IP.
sam_customer: we'll try 10min TTL and wire ElastiCache. Any security notes?
indra_runtime: longer TTL increases blast radius; recommended pattern: 10m access tokens backed by secure refresh flow or central broker for serverless. Shared cache is easiest quick win.
maggie_cs: opened CS-7021 to request temporary +500 concurrent window for 24h while they finish onboarding. Assign infra.
deploy-bot: node-sdk v1.2.1 scheduled with sessionCache and maxParallelRequests.
sam_customer: increased TTL to 600s and connected ElastiCache; reran test and 429s disappeared. Latency stabilized. Thanks!
maggie_cs: will document serverless token broker pattern in onboarding checklist and add Node snippet for devex. Closing unless issues.
